name: @kitora/spreadsheet
description: Kitora's spreadsheet grid in layers: a framework-free sheet model (addresses, a pluggable formula engine with dependency-ordered recalculation, selection, clipboard codecs, fill series, sort, undo), headless grid behaviour, unstyled React hooks, and styled compound parts (toolbar, formula bar, virtualised grid, status bar) with a preset built from them.

exports.description: The map key of one cell.

exports.name: keyAddr
exports.description: The inverse of {@link cellKey}.

exports.name: colName
exports.description: Column index → letters: 0 → A, 25 → Z, 26 → AA.

exports.name: colIndex
exports.description: Column letters → index (case-insensitive); -1 for anything that is not letters.

exports.name: parseAddr
exports.description: `"B3"` / `"$B$3"` → `{row: 2, col: 1}`; null when it is not a reference.

exports.name: parseRange
exports.description: `"A1:C3"` or a lone `"B2"` → a normalised range; null otherwise.

exports.name: rangeOf
exports.description: The normalised range spanned by two corners.

exports.name: rangeName
exports.description: `{r0:0,c0:0,r1:2,c1:2}` → `"A1:C3"`; a single cell prints as `"A1"`.

exports.name: inRange
exports.description: Whether the cell at `row`, `col` lies inside `range` (edges included).

exports.name: rangeRows

exports.name: rangeCols
exports.description: How many columns `range` spans.

exports.name: pasteTarget
exports.description:
Where a pasted block of `blockRows × blockCols` cells lands on the destination range `dest`: it starts at
`dest`'s top-left cell, is tiled when `dest` is a whole multiple of the block in that direction (one copy
otherwise, so a single selected cell takes the whole block), and is clipped to a `rows × cols` sheet. The cell
at (`row`, `col`) in the result takes the block's cell `[(row - r0) % blockRows][(col - c0) % blockCols]`.
Null for an empty block. The rule Excel and Sheets follow, shared by the spreadsheet store and the datagrid.
exports.signature: (dest: CellRange, blockRows: number, blockCols: number, rows: number, cols: number) => CellRange | null

exports.name: clampAddr
exports.description: Clamp a position into a `rows × cols` sheet.
exports.signature: (addr: CellAddr, rows: number, cols: number) => CellAddr

exports.name: CellAddr
exports.description: A zero-based cell position. Row 0 is sheet row 1, column 0 is column A.

exports.name: CellRange
exports.description: An inclusive, normalised rectangle (`r0 <= r1`, `c0 <= c1`).

exports.name: MAX_COLS
exports.description:
The widest sheet the key scheme supports (column XFD, Excel's limit). Keys are
`row * MAX_COLS + col`, so they stay unique whatever column count a sheet uses and
never need rewriting when a sheet grows.

exports.name: sheetError
exports.description: Makes the error value for `error`.

exports.name: isError
exports.description: Whether a computed value is an error rather than a number, text, boolean or blank.

exports.name: dateSerial

exports.name: serialToIso

exports.name: parseLiteral
exports.description:
Parse what a user typed into a constant. A leading apostrophe forces text
(`'0042` stays `"0042"`); formulas (`=…`) are the engine's job, not this one.

exports.name: createValueFormatter
exports.description: The default formatter, for a locale and currency of your choice. Errors, booleans and text print the same in every locale.

exports.name: formatValue
exports.description: The text a cell shows for `value` under `format` (falling back to the format the input implied), with the default formatter.
exports.signature: (value: CellValue, format?: CellFormat, inferred?: NumberFormat) => string

exports.name: defaultAlign
exports.description: Where a value sits in its cell when the format sets no alignment: numbers right, text left.

exports.name: sameFormat
exports.description: Two formats are equal when every field matches (absent and undefined are the same).
exports.signature: (a: CellFormat | undefined, b: CellFormat | undefined) => boolean

exports.name: compactFormat
exports.description: A format with its empty fields dropped; `undefined` when nothing is left.

exports.name: ERROR_CODES
exports.description: Every error a cell can show. `#CIRC!` marks a formula that depends on itself.

exports.name: ErrorCode
exports.description: One of `ERROR_CODES`.

exports.name: SheetError
exports.description: An error value a cell computes, such as `#DIV/0!`.

exports.name: CellValue
exports.description: A computed cell value. `null` is an empty cell.

exports.name: NUMBER_FORMATS
exports.description: The number formats the toolbar offers. `general` prints numbers as typed.

exports.name: NumberFormat
exports.description: One of `NUMBER_FORMATS`.

exports.name: ALIGNMENTS
exports.description: The horizontal alignments a cell can take.

exports.name: Align
exports.description: One of `ALIGNMENTS`.

exports.name: CellFormat
exports.description: Per-cell formatting. Every field is optional; absent means the default for the value's kind.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DECIMALS
exports.description: Fraction digits used when a format sets none (Excel's defaults).

exports.name: MAX_DECIMALS
exports.description: The most fraction digits the decimals buttons go to.

exports.name: ParsedLiteral
exports.description: A literal parsed from typed input, with the format the input implied ("12%" implies percent).

exports.name: LiteralParser
exports.description:
The seam that turns typed input (anything not starting with `=`) into a value. Swap it to
accept `1.234,5`, `15/10/2026` or your own literal kinds; the default is `parseLiteral`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_LOCALE
exports.description: Locale the default formatter prints numbers in.

exports.name: DEFAULT_CURRENCY
exports.description: ISO 4217 code the default formatter's currency format uses.

exports.name: ValueFormatter
exports.description:
The seam that turns a computed value into the text a cell shows. The store calls it for
every visible cell, so keep it cheap (cache `Intl` objects). Swap it to print another
locale or currency, a different date style, or your own number kinds; the default is
`createValueFormatter()`.

exports.name: ValueFormatterOptions
exports.description: Options for `createValueFormatter`: locale, currency and date style.

exports.name: defaultValueFormatter
exports.description: The formatter a store uses when the host passes none (en-US, USD, ISO dates).

exports.name: isFormula
exports.description: True when cell input is a formula (`=` followed by something).

exports.name: parseFormula
exports.description: Parse cell input that starts with `=`.

exports.name: collectRefs
exports.description: Every cell and range a parsed formula reads, for dependency tracking.

exports.name: refSpans
exports.description: The references in a formula's text with their offsets (offsets count the leading `=`). Empty when it does not lex.

exports.name: shiftFormula
exports.description:
Move a formula by `dRow` / `dCol` the way copying it does: relative parts shift,
`$` parts stay. A reference pushed off the sheet's top or left edge becomes `#REF!`.
Text that does not lex is returned unchanged.
exports.signature: (input: string, dRow: number, dCol: number) => string

exports.name: isRangeArg
exports.description: Whether a function argument is a range (its values flattened) rather than a single value.
exports.signature: (a: FunctionArg) => a is { readonly range: readonly CellValue[]; }

exports.name: toNumber
exports.description: Coerce a value to a number as arithmetic does: blank is 0, TRUE is 1, numeric text parses, other text is `#VALUE!`.

exports.name: toBool
exports.description: Coerce a value to a boolean as `IF`/`AND` do: numbers are truthy when non-zero, "TRUE"/"FALSE" text parses.

exports.name: toText
exports.description: Coerce a value to text as `&` does (numbers print with 15 significant digits).

exports.name: numbersOf
exports.description:
Numbers an aggregate reads: ranges contribute their numbers only (text, booleans
and blanks are skipped, as in Excel); a direct argument is coerced. Returns the
first error met.

exports.name: scalar
exports.description: A direct (non-range) argument's value; a range where one value is expected is `#VALUE!`, a missing one is blank.

exports.name: evaluate
exports.description: Evaluate a parsed formula against the sheet. Never throws; problems come back as error values.

exports.name: RefSpec
exports.description: One reference as written: where it points and which parts carry a `$`.

exports.name: FormulaNode
exports.description: A node of a parsed formula's syntax tree, told apart by `k` (number, text, reference, range, operator, call…).

exports.name: ParsedFormula
exports.description: A parsed formula, or the reason it does not parse (the cell then shows `#ERROR!` / `#NAME?`).

exports.name: FormulaRefs
exports.description: Every cell a formula reads: single references and ranges, kept apart so a range never expands.

exports.name: RefSpan
exports.description: A reference's position in the source text, for highlighting while editing.

exports.name: FunctionArg
exports.description:
One argument a function receives: a scalar, or a range's values flattened row by row
(`{ range }`), so an aggregate can skip text in ranges but coerce a direct argument, as Excel does.

exports.name: SheetFunction
exports.description:
A spreadsheet function: evaluated arguments in, a value out. Never throw; return an
error value (`sheetError("#VALUE!")`) instead. Arguments are evaluated eagerly, so a
lazy function like `IF` cannot be written this way (it is built into the evaluator).

exports.name: FunctionTable
exports.description: Functions by UPPER-CASE name (the lexer upper-cases what the user types).

exports.name: EvalContext
exports.description: How the evaluator reads the sheet.

exports.name: aggregate
exports.description: Build an aggregate (SUM-like) function from what it does with the numbers its arguments hold.

exports.name: BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS
exports.description: The built-in functions, by upper-case name. Spread it into your own table to extend or override it.

exports.name: FUNCTION_NAMES
exports.description: The functions the engine knows, for autocomplete and docs. `IF` is evaluated lazily, so it is not in the table.

exports.name: functionTable
exports.description: The function table an engine resolves calls against for `options`, names upper-cased.

exports.name: CellData
exports.description: What a cell stores: the raw input (a literal or `=formula`) and its format.

exports.name: CellWrite
exports.description: One write: `cell: undefined` deletes the cell.

exports.name: EngineOptions
exports.description: The engine's seams. Every one is optional; the defaults are the built-in functions and `parseLiteral`.

exports.name: SheetEngine
exports.description:
The formula engine behind a sheet: holds every cell's input and format, parses formulas, tracks which cells
depend on which, and recomputes only the affected values after a write. No DOM, no React.

exports.name: toTsv
exports.description: Rows of fields → TSV text (no trailing newline).

exports.name: parseTsv
exports.description:
TSV text → rows of fields. Accepts `\n` and `\r\n`, quoted fields with embedded
tabs, newlines and doubled quotes, and drops the one trailing newline most apps add.

exports.name: ClipboardCodec
tsvCodec
exports.description: The default clipboard codec: tab-separated values with quoting.

exports.name: fillLane
exports.description:
The cells a fill writes for one lane. `offsets` are positions relative to the
source's first cell (`n, n+1, …` going down or right; `-1, -2, …` going up or left).
`axis` says how one offset step moves a formula: by rows or by columns.
exports.signature: (source: readonly (CellData | undefined)[], offsets: readonly number[], axis: "row" | "col") => (CellData | undefined)[]

exports.name: FILL_DIRECTIONS
exports.description: Which way the handle was dragged.

exports.name: FillDirection
exports.description: One of `FILL_DIRECTIONS`: the way a fill-handle drag went.

exports.name: compareValues
exports.description: Compare two values ascending; blanks are not handled here (see {@link sortOrder}).

exports.name: sortOrder
exports.description: The order rows should take: `keys[i]` is row i's sort value; returns the old row indices in new order.

exports.name: SORT_DIRECTIONS
exports.description: The ways a sort runs: `asc` for A→Z, `desc` for Z→A.

exports.name: SortDirection
exports.description: One of `SORT_DIRECTIONS`.

exports.name: fillTarget
exports.description: The range a fill drag covers, or null while the pointer is still inside the source.
exports.signature: (source: CellRange, hover: CellAddr) => { readonly range: CellRange; readonly direction: FillDirection; } | null

exports.name: Selection
exports.description: The selection: ranges in click order (the last one is current), the cell typing goes to, and the corner Shift moves.

exports.name: EDIT_MODES
exports.description: `enter`: typing replaced the cell and arrows commit and move. `edit` (F2, double-click): arrows move the caret.

exports.name: EditMode
exports.description: One of `EDIT_MODES`.

exports.name: EDIT_ORIGINS
exports.description: Where the edit is typed: in the cell or in the formula bar.

exports.name: EditOrigin
exports.description: One of `EDIT_ORIGINS`.

exports.name: EditState

props.name: mode
props.description: Whether arrows commit and move (`enter`) or move the caret (`edit`).

props.name: origin

exports.name: Freeze
exports.description: Frozen panes: how many top rows and left columns stay put while the rest scrolls.

exports.name: MOVE_DIRECTIONS
exports.description: Directions a commit or a keyboard move goes.

exports.name: MoveDirection
exports.description: One of `MOVE_DIRECTIONS`.

exports.name: SpreadsheetState
exports.description: The immutable snapshot React renders from. A new object after every change.

props.name: cols

props.name: colWidths

props.name: selection

props.name: canRedo

exports.description: Defaults a sheet starts with when the host passes nothing.

exports.name: HISTORY_LIMIT
exports.description: How many steps undo remembers; older steps fall off.

exports.name: CHANGE_SOURCES
exports.description: What started a data change: a user action, history, or a host `load`.

exports.name: ChangeSource
exports.description: One of `CHANGE_SOURCES`.

exports.name: SheetChange
exports.description: One data change: the cells written (`cell: undefined` = cleared) and what caused it.

exports.name: CellRecord
exports.description: Cells by A1 address, the shape `cells` init, `toCells` and `load` share. A string is an input without a format.

exports.name: SpreadsheetInit
exports.description: What a new `SpreadsheetStore` starts with: size, widths, frozen panes, cells, formatter and clipboard codec, plus the engine options.

exports.name: CellDisplay
exports.description: What a cell shows: text plus the presentation the grid needs.

exports.name: FORMAT_FLAGS
exports.description: A boolean format flag the toolbar toggles.

exports.name: FormatFlag
exports.description: One of `FORMAT_FLAGS`.

exports.name: SpreadsheetStore
exports.description:
A sheet's state machine: cells and values (through its `SheetEngine`), selection, the edit in progress, column
widths, frozen panes, clipboard and undo/redo. Every user action is a method; React reads it through
`subscribe` / `getState`.

exports.name: GUTTER_WIDTH
exports.description: Width of the row-number gutter, px (fits "10000").

exports.name: HEADER_HEIGHT
exports.description: Height of the column-letter header row, px.

exports.name: OVERSCAN_COLS
exports.description: Extra columns rendered past each edge, so fast scrolling never shows blank strips.

exports.name: OVERSCAN_ROWS
exports.description: Extra rows and columns rendered past each edge, so fast scrolling never shows blank strips.

exports.name: columnAt
exports.description: The column whose span contains `x` (clamped to the sheet).

exports.name: columnLefts
exports.description: `lefts[c]` is column c's left edge from the first column; `lefts[cols]` is the total width.

exports.name: sameViewport
exports.description: Whether two viewports cover the same rows and columns.

exports.name: visibleWindow
exports.description:
Rows and columns of the scrolling (non-frozen) area on screen for a scroll position,
widened by the overscan. Frozen rows/columns are always rendered, so they are excluded.
exports.signature: (opts: { readonly scrollTop: number; readonly scrollLeft: number; readonly width: number; readonly height: number; readonly rowHeight: number; readonly rows: number; readonly lefts: readonly number[]; readonly freezeRows: number; readonly freezeCols: number; }) => Viewport

exports.name: Viewport
exports.description: The visible slice of a sheet: inclusive first/last row and column in the scrolling area.

exports.name: trackPointer
exports.description: Call `move` on every pointer move and `up` once on release, on the window. Returns a function that stops tracking early.
exports.signature: (move: (e: PointerEvent) => void, up?: (e: PointerEvent) => void) => () => void

exports.name: DEFAULT_MEASURE_FONT
exports.description: Font the default measurer uses; matches the styled grid's cell text (13px, system sans).

exports.name: FALLBACK_CHAR_WIDTH
exports.description: Average glyph width the measurer falls back to when no canvas context exists (px per character).

exports.name: canvasTextMeasurer
exports.description: A measurer that draws on one off-screen canvas, created on first use.

exports.name: TextMeasurer
exports.description: Width in px of `text` as a cell draws it (`bold` cells are wider).

exports.name: bindClipboard
exports.description: Route the document's copy / cut / paste to `target` while `owns()` is true. Returns the cleanup.
exports.signature: (doc: Document, target: ClipboardTarget, owns: () => boolean) => () => void

exports.name: ClipboardTarget
exports.description:
What `bindClipboard` routes the clipboard to: the `SpreadsheetStore` satisfies it as is, and the datagrid's
cell clipboard is another. `copy` returns the clipboard text (`cut` is true for a cut event), or `null` when
there is nothing to copy, which leaves the event to the browser. `paste` takes the clipboard text; returning
`false` says it took nothing (a read-only grid, say), which also leaves the event to the browser.

exports.name: GRID_KEY_BINDINGS
exports.description: The default table: the Excel / Sheets keys. Order matters only between overlapping chords (the first match wins).

exports.name: defaultGridKeymap
exports.description: Excel / Sheets keys: `GRID_KEY_BINDINGS` plus typing to replace.
exports.signature: (stroke: KeyStroke, store: SpreadsheetStore, ctx: GridKeyContext) => boolean

exports.name: gridKeymap
exports.description:
Compile a binding table into a keymap. Bindings are parsed once, here (a malformed one throws the
keyboard kit's `BindingParseError` at once, not on the first key press); each must be one chord.

exports.name: typeToEdit
exports.description: The default fallback: a printable character typed without Ctrl/Cmd/Alt (AltGr characters count) replaces the cell.
exports.signature: (stroke: KeyStroke, store: SpreadsheetStore, ctx: GridKeyContext) => boolean

exports.name: GridKeyBinding
exports.description: One grid shortcut: a keyboard-kit binding string (one chord) and what it does. `run` returning false leaves the key to the browser.

exports.name: GridKeyContext
exports.description: What the grid gives a keymap besides the store.

exports.name: GridKeyFallback
exports.description: What runs when no binding matched (the default types into the cell).

exports.name: GridKeymap
exports.description: Handle one key press; true when handled (the caller prevents the default).

exports.name: useSheetState

exports.description: The surrounding `<SpreadsheetProvider>`'s store and grid handle. Throws outside one.

exports.description: The context `SpreadsheetProvider` fills with its store and grid handle; read it with `useSpreadsheetContext`.

exports.name: GridApi
exports.description: What the mounted grid lets its neighbours do.

exports.name: SpreadsheetContextValue
exports.description: What the parts around a grid share. `api` is filled once the grid mounts.

exports.name: SpreadsheetControl
exports.description:
Optional control over a `useSpreadsheet` store's cells. Leave `cells` out and the store
owns them (uncontrolled; `onCellsChange` still reports). Pass `cells` and the host owns
them: every user change is reported through `onCellsChange`, and whenever the host passes
a `cells` object other than the one it was last given, the sheet is replaced by it.
